translations.text: In the twelfth year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, who reigned over Assyria in the great city of Nineveh, in the days of Arphaxad, who reigned over the Medes in Ecbatana,
he built a wall of hewn stones around it, each stone three cubits long and six cubits wide. The height of the wall was seventy cubits, and its width was fifty cubits.
He raised its towers above its gates to a hundred cubits, and he laid the foundations of their width at sixty cubits.
He made its gates tall gates, seventy cubits high and forty cubits wide, so that his army of mighty men, his chariots and his ranks of foot soldiers could march out.
In those days Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Assyrians, made war against King Arphaxad on the plain, that is, in the territory of Ragau.

All the people who lived along the Euphrates, the Tigris and the Hydaspes joined him for battle, together with those of the plain of Arioch, who belong to the king of the Elymaeans. Many nations gathered to draw up in battle order against the sons of Cheleoud.

Nebuchadnezzar, king of Assyria, sent messengers to all who lived in Persia and to all who lived in the west, to those who lived in Cilicia, Damascus and Lebanon, and to all who lived along the seacoast,
and to the nations of Carmel, upper Galilee and the great plain of Esdraelon,
and to those who lived in Samaria and its cities, beyond the Jordan, as far as Jerusalem and Betane, as far as the river of Egypt, Tahpanhes and Raamses,
and to all the land of Goshen, as far as upper Tanis and Memphis, and to all who lived in Egypt, as far as the borders of Ethiopia.

But all the people of the land ignored the word of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Assyria, and did not join him in the war, because they were not afraid of him. To them he was like any other man, their equal, and they sent his messengers back empty-handed and in disgrace.

Nebuchadnezzar became very angry with that whole land, and he swore by his throne and his kingdom that he would take revenge on all the territories of Cilicia, Damascus and Assyria, and destroy with his sword all who lived in Moab, the sons of Ammon, all Judah, and all the people of Egypt, as far as the borders of the two seas.

In the seventeenth year he drew up his army in battle order against King Arphaxad, king of the Medes. He prevailed in battle and routed Arphaxad's whole army, with all his cavalry and all his chariots.
He took possession of his cities and advanced as far as Ecbatana. There he seized its tower, plundered its streets and turned its beauty into a disgrace.
He captured Arphaxad, ran him through with a spear in the mountains of Ragau, and destroyed him with his lances, once and for all.

Then he returned with them to Nineveh, with his whole army and all the forces gathered to him, a very great multitude of warriors. He and all his army stayed there at ease for a hundred and twenty days.
In the eighteenth year, on the twenty-second day of the first month, it was decided in the house of Nebuchadnezzar to take revenge on the whole land, as he had said.
And he summoned all his servants and all his great men, and laid before them the secret of his counsel. And it came to pass, when he had finished speaking all his evil counsel against that land,
that they decreed to destroy all the land that had not obeyed the words of his mouth.
And it came to pass, when he had completed his counsels, that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Assyria, summoned by word Holofernes, the general of his army, who was second to him, and said to him:

"Thus says the great king, the lord of all the earth: Behold, you shall go out from my presence and take with you men who trust in their strength: a hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and a multitude of horses and horsemen, twelve myriads.
And go out to make war on all the land of the west, because they have disobeyed the words of my mouth;

and tell them to prepare earth and water for me, for I am going out against them in my anger. And I will cover the whole face of the earth with the feet of my army, and I will give them over to them to be plundered.
And their valleys and all their ravines shall be filled with their wounded, and the rivers shall sweep away their dead and be filled with them,
and I will carry off their captives to the ends of the earth.
But you, go out and seize all their territories for me in advance, and they shall give themselves up to you, and you shall keep them for me until the day of their punishment.
But as for those who do not obey you, let your eye not spare them from being given over to death and to plunder in all the land,
for I live, and so does the power of my kingdom. As I have spoken, so I will do all this by my hand.
And you shall not transgress a single word of your lord, but carry it out fully, as I have commanded you, and do not delay in doing it."
And Holofernes went out from the presence of his lord, and summoned all the mighty men, the commanders, the officers, and the overseers of the army of Assyria.
And he counted out chosen men for battle, as his lord had commanded him: twelve myriads of horsemen, and two myriads and two thousand archers.
And he organized them in the manner in which a multitude of warriors is ordered, and set them in array.
And he brought camels and mules and donkeys for their baggage, a very great multitude, and cattle and sheep and goats beyond number for their food;
and provisions for every man in abundance, and a very great quantity of gold and silver from the royal house.
And he went out from Nineveh, he and all his army, to march ahead of King Nebuchadnezzar and to cover the whole face of the earth toward the west with chariots and horsemen and chosen foot soldiers.
And a great mixed multitude joined them, like locusts and like the sand of the sea in number, for their multitude could not be counted.
And they went out from Nineveh a three days' journey toward the plain of Bectileth, near the mountain on the upper side of Cilicia.
And he took all his army, the foot soldiers, the horsemen, and the chariots, and went from there toward the hill country.

And he destroyed the people of Put and Lud, and plundered all the children of Rassis and the children of Ishmael, who lived along the edge of the desert, to the south of the land of Cheleon and of the Chaldeans.
And he crossed the Euphrates and passed through Mesopotamia, and he destroyed the high cities along the ravine of Abrona until he came to the Great Sea.
And he seized the territory of Cilicia and slaughtered everyone who resisted him, and he reached the borders of Japheth in the south, facing Arabia.
And he surrounded all the sons of Midian, burned all their tents, and carried off their plunder.

And he came down into the plain of Damascus in the days of the wheat harvest. He burned all their fields and ravaged their plains. He handed over their [?], their flocks and their herds to destruction, plundered their cities, scattered their farmland, and killed all their young men with the edge of the sword.

And fear and trembling of him fell on the people who lived along the seacoast, those who were in Sidon and Tyre, and on the people of Sur and the land beyond it, and on the people of Jamnia, Azotus, Gaza and Ascalon, and they were very much afraid.

And they sent messengers to him with words of peace, and they said: And the sons of Israel who lived in Judea heard all that Holofernes, the general of Nebuchadnezzar king of Assyria, had done to the nations of the earth, and how he had plundered all their shrines and given them over to destruction.

"Here we are, servants of Nebuchadnezzar the great king, before you. Make use of us as seems good to you." And they were very much afraid of him, and they were terrified for Jerusalem and for the temple of the Lord their God.

"Here are our dwellings, and those who live in them are your servants. All our wheat fields, our flocks and herds, and all the encampments of our [?] are before you; use them as seems good to you." For they had only just come back from captivity, and the vessels, the altar and the temple had only just been purified from their defilement.
"Come and take possession of them as you wish." And they sent word to the sons of Israel, to all the territory of Samaria, Kona, Beroe, Belmain, Jericho, Choba, Eora, and the valleys of Jerusalem.

And the men came to Holofernes and told him these words. And they seized all the tops of the high mountains, walled their villages, and stored food in them to prepare for war, because their fields had just been harvested.

And he came down to the seacoast, he and all his army, and surrounded their cities, and he took strong men from them for war. And Joakim the high priest, who was in Jerusalem in those days, wrote to the people of Bethulia and of the district of Betomesthaim, which is opposite Esdraelon, facing the plain that lies before Dothaim, from Masadan toward Brion,

and they welcomed him, together with all their villages, with garlands, dances and timbrels. And he told them: "Seize the mountain passes, because through them lay the way into Judea." And it was easy to stop anyone from coming, because the pass was narrow, wide enough for only two men.

And they destroyed all their borders and cut down all their groves. For he had been given a command to destroy all the idols of the land, so that all nations and all tongues would serve Nebuchadnezzar alone, and their tribes would call on him as god by their [?]. And the sons of Israel did as Joakim the high priest and all the elders of the people of Israel who were in Jerusalem had commanded them.
And he came opposite Esdraelon, near Dothan, which faces the great ridge of Judea. And all Israel cried out to God with great earnestness, and they humbled their souls with fasting.

And they encamped between Geba and Scythopolis, which is Gebana [?], and he stayed there one month so that his whole army could gather there. They, their wives, their infants, and even their cattle, and every foreigner living among them, every hired worker, and every slave bought with their silver put sackcloth around their waists.
And every man and woman, and the children who lived in Jerusalem, fell down before the temple, poured ashes on their heads, and spread out their sackcloth before the Lord.

And they draped the altar in sackcloth, and with one voice they cried out with all their heart to the God of Israel not to hand their infants over to be seized, their wives to be carried off as captives, the cities of their inheritance to be destroyed, or the sanctuary to be defiled, mocked and made something for the gentiles to gloat over.
And the Lord heard their voice and saw their affliction. And the people fasted for many days throughout Judea and in Jerusalem before the sanctuary of the Lord Almighty.

And Joakim the high priest and all who stood before the Lord, the priests and ministers of the Lord, with sackcloth around their waists, offered their regular burnt offerings, along with the prayers and the freewill offerings of the people,
and ashes had been poured on their turbans. And they cried out to the Lord with all their heart and all their strength, asking the Lord to look with favour on the whole house of Israel.

And Holofernes, the commander of the Assyrian army, was told that the sons of Israel had prepared for war. They had closed off the mountain passes, fortified all the summits of the high mountains, and put obstacles on the plains.
And he became very angry and summoned all the princes of Moab, the commanders of Ammon, and all the governors of the seacoast.

And he said to them: "Tell me, sons of Canaan, who is this people that lives in the mountains? And who are the people living in their cities? How large is their army? What is their strength and their might? And what king has risen over them as leader of their people?
And why did they not listen to me and come out to meet me, as all the inhabitants of the west did?"

Achior, the leader of the sons of Ammon, answered him and said: "Let my lord hear a word from the mouth of your servant, and I will tell you the truth about the people who live in these mountains near you. No lie will come out of your servant's mouth.
This people is descended from the Chaldeans.
And they first lived as sojourners in Mesopotamia, because they did not want to follow the gods of their fathers, who were glorified in the land of the Chaldeans.

And they left the ways of their kindred and worshipped the God of heaven, the God whom they had come to know. And they brought them out from the presence of their gods, and they fled to Mesopotamia and lived there as sojourners for many days.
And God told them to leave the place where they were sojourning and to come to the land of Canaan. And they dwelt there two hundred and fifteen years and grew very rich in gold, silver and livestock.

And they went down to Egypt, because famine covered the face of all the land, and again they lived there as sojourners for two hundred and fifteen years, until they grew and became a great multitude there; and there was no counting the multitude of their people.
And the king of Egypt rose up against them and oppressed them with hard labour and brick-making. They humbled their multitude and enslaved them.

And they cried out to their God, and their God struck Egypt with torments on their account. And he destroyed all the land of Egypt with plagues for which there was no cure, and they drove them out of Egypt from before them.
And God dried up the Red Sea before them.
And he brought them to Mount Sinai and the road of Kadesh-barnea, and they drove out all the inhabitants of the wilderness.
And they settled in the land of the Amorites and destroyed all the people of Heshbon by their strength. And they crossed the Jordan and took possession of all this hill country.
And they drove out the Canaanites from before them, and likewise the Perizzites, the Jebusites, Shechem and the Girgashites, and they dwelt among them for many days.
As long as they did not sin before their God, things went well for them, because God, who hates falsehood, is with them.

But when they turned away from the way that the law had set for them, they were destroyed in many battles over a very long time and were carried off as captives to a foreign land. The temple of their God was laid waste, and their cities were seized by their enemies.

And now they have returned to their God and have come back from the dispersion in which they had been scattered. They have again taken possession of Jerusalem, where their sanctuary is, and they have settled in the hill country, because it had been laid waste.

And now, sovereign lord, if there is any error among that people and they are sinning against their God, then let us see that this is a stumbling block for them, and let us go up and fight against them.
But if there is no lawlessness among them and their people, then let my lord pass them by, lest the Lord their God help them and we become a reproach before the whole earth.

And when Achior finished speaking these words, all the people standing around Holofernes's tent murmured and surrounded him. And Holofernes's commanders and all the inhabitants of the seacoast said that he should be destroyed.
"For we are not afraid of the sons of Israel. They are a people who have no power and no strength to draw up a mighty force for battle.
So now let us go up into the mountains, and they will be food for us and for all your people, lord Holofernes!"
And when the uproar of those men died down, Holofernes the commander said to Achior the Samaritan, before all the people of the foreigners:

"And who are you, Achior, along with all the sons of Ammon and the hirelings of Ephraim, that you prophesied among us as you have today, and said that the race of the sons of Israel is not to be fought, because their God will help them? And who is God, if not Nebuchadnezzar? He will send his might and destroy them from the face of the earth as one man, and their God will not be able to save them.
"But we, his servants, will cut them down as one man, and they will not withstand the multitude of our horses.

"For we will sweep them away with them [?], and their borders will be drunk with their blood, and their plains will be filled with their corpses. Not even the track of their feet will stand before our face; they will utterly perish, says King Nebuchadnezzar, lord of all the earth. For he has spoken, and the words of his mouth will not be made void.

"But you, Achior, hireling of Ammon, who spoke those words on this day of your falsehood, you will not see my face again from this day until I take vengeance on that people and its race that came out of Egypt.
"And then the sword of my servants will pass through your sides, and you will fall among their wounded when I return.
"And my servants will take you back on that day toward the hill country and leave you in one of the cities of the ascents.
"And you will see everything, and only then will you perish with them.
"And if you hope in your heart that I will not be able to capture them, do not let your face be downcast. I have spoken, and none of these words of mine will fail."
And Holofernes commanded his servants who stood before his tent to seize Achior and take him to Bethulia, into the hands of the sons of Israel.
And his servants seized him, led him outside the camp, and took him from there toward the hill country, and they came to the springs that are below Bethulia.

And when the men of the city saw them on the top of the mountain, they took up their weapons and went out of the city onto the mountain, and every slinger held the ascent against them and hurled stones at them.
And they took cover below the mountain and withdrew, and they bound Achior and left him lying there and went back to their lord.
And the sons of Israel came down and untied him, brought him into Bethulia, and presented him to the rulers of the city
who were in office in those days. These were Uzziah son of Micah, of the tribe of Simeon, Chabris son of Othniel, and Charmis son of Melchiel.
And they summoned all the elders of the city, and all their young men, their women, and their children gathered to their assembly. And Uzziah questioned him about what had happened to him.

And Achior told them what had been said in the council of Holofernes, and all the words of the commanders of the sons of the Assyrians, everything they had said, and what great boasts Holofernes had spoken against the house of Israel.
And the people fell down, worshipped God, cried out, and said:
"O Lord God of heaven and earth, look down upon their arrogance and have mercy on the lowliness of our race, and look this day upon the faces of those consecrated to you!"
And they comforted Achior and praised him greatly, and said to him: "As it pleases God, so may it also be well with you."
And Uzziah took him from the assembly to his own house and held a feast with the elders, and they called upon the Lord all night.
And on the next day Holofernes commanded all his army, and all the valiant men who had come to help him, to go up to Bethulia, seize the ascents of the mountains, and make war on the sons of Israel.

And every strong man armed himself on that day. The strong men, all the warriors, were one hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers and twenty-two thousand horsemen. This was apart from their baggage and the men on foot who were among them, a very great multitude.

And they encamped in the valley near Bethulia, by the spring, and spread out in breadth toward Dothaim and as far as Balbaim, and in length from Bethulia as far as Cyamon, which is opposite Esdraelon.

But when the sons of Israel saw their multitude, they were greatly troubled, and each man said to his neighbour: “Now these men will wipe out the face of the earth. Neither the high mountains nor the hills nor the ravines will withstand this great multitude of theirs.”
And each man took up his weapons of war, and they lit fires on the towers of their walls, and they stood and guarded their walls that night.
And on the second day Holofernes led out all his horsemen before the face of the sons of Israel who were in Bethulia,
and he surveyed the ascents of their mountain and of their city. He went around the springs of water, seized them, and set camps of fighting men over them, and he himself rode back to his army.
And all the chiefs of the sons of Israel, all the leaders of the people of Moab, and the governors of the seacoast came to him and said:
“Let our lord hear our word, so that there may be no stumbling for your army.
For this people of the sons of Israel do not trust in their spears. They trust in the height of the mountains on which they dwell, for it is very difficult to go up against them.
And now, lord, do not fight them in battle array, and not even one man of your people will fall.
Wait, stay in your camp, and keep every man of your force within the camp. Let your servants seize the springs of water that come out from the foot of the mountain.

For all the inhabitants of Bethulia draw their water from there, and thirst will destroy them, and they will give up their city to us. And we and your people will go up near the tops of the mountains, encamp on them, and keep watch over them, so that not even one man can come out of their city.
And they, their wives, and their children will perish by hunger, and before the sword reaches them they will fall in the streets of their dwellings.
And they will be repaid with an evil recompense for this, because they rebelled and did not come out to meet your face in peace.”
And these words of theirs pleased Holofernes and all his servants, and they ordered that it be done as they had said.
And the camp of the sons of Ammon set out, and with them five thousand Assyrian foot soldiers. They encamped in the valley and seized all the waters and the springs of water of the sons of Israel.

And the sons of Esau and the sons of Moab went up and encamped on the mountain opposite Dothan. They led them off toward the south and toward the sunrise, opposite the place of assembly near Cush, which is by the valley of Bochor. And the rest of the Assyrian army spread out and encamped on the plain. They covered the face of all the land of Kedar. With their tents and their baggage they encamped as a great host, for they were very great in number.
And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord their God, for their spirit failed them. Their enemies had surrounded them on every side, and there was no way of escape from among them.

For they surrounded them and held their whole territory. The whole camp of the Assyrians, with their chariots and their horsemen, stayed there for thirty-two days, and all the water supplies of the inhabitants of Bethulia ran out.
And their cisterns were becoming empty. For many days they did not have enough water to drink their fill, because it was given to them to drink by measure.

And the people lost heart, along with their infants, their wives and their young men. They grew faint with thirst and collapsed in the streets of their city and in the passageways of the gates, and there was no strength left in them.
And all the people gathered around Uzziah and the rulers of the city: young men, women and children. They cried out with a loud voice before all the elders and said:
"May God judge between us and you! You have done us a great injustice, because you did not speak peaceably with the sons of Assyria.
"And there is no one to help us. Instead, God has delivered us into their hands, to fall before them from thirst.
"And now send to them and call them, and hand over this whole city as plunder to the people of Holofernes and to all his army.

"For it is better for us to become their spoil than to perish like this. Let us become their slaves and maidservants, and our souls will live. Then we will not see our infants die before our eyes, nor our wives and children breathe their last.

"We call heaven and earth to witness against you, and our God, the Lord of our fathers, who is punishing us for our sins and for the falsehoods of our fathers, so that he may not act according to their words this very day."
And there was great weeping in the midst of the assembly from everyone together, and they cried out to the Lord their God with a loud voice.
And Uzziah said to them: "Do not be afraid, brothers. Let us hold out for just five more days, until the Lord God turns his mercy toward us, for he will not forsake us completely.
"If these days pass and no help comes to us from anywhere, then we will do as you say."
And the people dispersed, each to his own post, each man going to the walls and towers of the city. He sent their wives and children to their houses, and they were in great humiliation in the city.

And in those days Judith heard of it. She was the daughter of Merari, son of Ochozias, son of Joseph, son of Oziel, son of Hilkiah, son of Ananias, son of Gideon, son of Raphain, son of Ahitub, son of Elijah, son of Hilkiah, son of Enab, son of Nathanael, son of Salamiel, son of Sarad, son of Simeon, son of Israel.
Her husband Manasseh was of her tribe and of her own family. Manasseh died at the very time of the barley harvest.

For he was standing over the reapers in the field of sheaves, and the heat struck his head. He lay down on his bed and died in Bethulia, his city. They buried him in his city with his fathers, in the field between Dothan and Balamon.
Judith lived as a widow in her house for three years and six months.
She made a tent on the roof of her house and put sackcloth around her waist.
She wore the garments of her widowhood. She fasted every day of her widowhood except the sabbaths, the new moons, the feasts, the days of rejoicing and the commemorations of the house of Israel.

She was fair to look upon and very beautiful of face, wise of heart and good of understanding, and very rich. For Manasseh her husband had left her gold and silver, menservants and maidservants, livestock and estates, and she remained in charge of them.
No one had heard an evil word spoken about her, for she feared God greatly.

These evil words of the people against the rulers were heard, for they had lost heart because of the lack of water. Judith heard all the words that Uzziah had spoken to the people, and how he had sworn to them that he would hand the city over to the Assyrians after five days.
She sent her maidservant, who was in charge of and managed all her possessions, and summoned Uzziah the priest, and Chabris and Charmis, the elders of her city.

They came to her, and she said to them: "Listen to me, you rulers of the inhabitants of Bethulia. This word of yours is not right, the word you spoke before the people today and confirmed with the oath you pronounced between God and yourselves. You promised to hand the city of our God over to our enemies unless God turns to help you within these days.
"And now who are you, that you should test the Lord God of Israel this very day? For you have set down a word about God among the sons of men.
"And now you are testing the Lord Almighty, and you will never understand anything, forever.

"For you cannot know the depth of a man's heart, and you cannot reach the reasoning of his mind. How then will you grasp the thoughts of God, who made all these things? He alone knows what he has planned for you. Will you know his mind and search out his counsels? No, brothers, no! Do not anger the Lord our God.

"If he does not wish to help us within these five days, he has the power by his own will to protect us in whatever days he wishes. He knows. Or he may destroy us before our enemies, for the power belongs to him too. And who will say to him, 'What is this you have done?'
"But do not test the counsel of the Lord our God. For God is not like a man, that anyone could accuse him, nor like a son of man, that anyone could treat him with contempt.
"Therefore let us wait for salvation from him and call upon him to help us. He will hear our voice if it is pleasing to him."
For there has not arisen among our generations, nor is there in this present day, any tribe, family, assembly or city of ours that worships idols made by hands, as there was in those former days.
Because of that sin our fathers were handed over to the sword of the Babylonians and to plunder for seventy years, and they fell with a great fall before their enemies.
But we know no other God besides him. We trust in him, that he will not disregard us and will not take his salvation and his mercy away from us and from our race.
For if we turn back, then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the land will stand as they are. Our holiness will be confirmed and made manifest, and God will require their blood for our defilement,

and for the slaughter of our brothers, the captivity of our land and the desolation of our inheritance. He will bring it back upon us among the nations, where we served them, and we were a stumbling-block and a reproach before all who took us captive.
For our servitude will not turn out to our favour but to our dishonour, and the Lord our God will appoint it so.
And now, brothers, let us set an example for our brothers, because their souls hang upon us, and the sanctuary and the temple of prayer are established among us.
For all this let us give thanks to the Lord our God, who is testing us as he tested our fathers.
Remember how much he did to Abraham, how he tested Isaac, and how much happened to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Assyria while he was tending the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother.

He tried them with fire to test their hearts. In the same way the Lord chastises us, those who are near to him, not in vengeance but for instruction. He is blessed and praised at all times forever. Amen!
And Uzziah said to her: "All that you have said, you have spoken with a good heart, and there is no one who will oppose your words.
For your wisdom is not made manifest only today. From the first days all the people have known your understanding, because what your heart forms is good.
But this people was very thirsty. They compelled us to speak as we spoke to them, and they brought upon us an oath that we cannot break.
Pray to the Lord for us, for you are a God-fearing woman, and the Lord will send rain so that our cisterns may be filled and we will no longer be in want."
And Judith said to them: "Listen to me, and let us do a deed of wisdom that will be told from generation to generation to the sons of our race.
Stand at the gate this day and night, and I will go out with my maidservant. Within the days after which you said you would hand this city over to the enemy, God will visit Israel by my hand.
But do not inquire into what I am doing, for I will not tell you until what I am going to do has been done and accomplished."
And Uzziah and the rulers said to her: "Go in peace, and may the Lord God be with you to take vengeance on our enemies."
And they went back from her tent, and each of them went away to his appointed place.

But Judith fell on her face, poured ashes on her head and took off the sackcloth that covered her body. It was just the time when the evening incense was being offered in Jerusalem in the house of the Lord. Judith cried out in a loud voice and said to the Lord God:

"O Lord God of my father Simeon, you gave a sword into his hand to take vengeance on the foreigners. They had loosened a virgin's womb to defile her, and stripped her body bare to defile, shame and disgrace her. For you said, 'It shall not be so.' This was because they had committed lawlessness against the virgin's blood.

And you gave their rulers over to slaughter. You gave over their bed, on which they had committed their deceit, which was deceived into blood. Slaves were struck down by the mighty, and the mighty [?] on their thrones.

And you gave their wives over to captivity and their daughters to be carried off. You gave all their goods to be divided among the sons you loved, who were zealous with your zeal. They loathed the defilement of their blood and called on you as their helper. O God of my father Simeon, of Levi, God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, O God, my God, hear me, a widow [?].
For you made what came before them and what came after. You planned what is now and what is to come, and it came to pass.
You called, and the things you had planned stood before you and said, 'Behold, here we are.' For all your ways are prepared, and your judgments are foreknowledge.

For behold, the Assyrians have multiplied in their might. They are exalted with horses and horsemen, and they boast in the arm of their foot soldiers. They trust in spears and [?], and they have set their hearts on bow and sling. They do not know that you are the God who crushes wars.

'The Lord' is your name. Cast down their multitude by your power, and strike down their strength in your anger. For they have planned to defile your sanctuary, to pollute the dwelling place of your name and the resting place of your glory, and to cast down the horn of your altar.
Look upon their arrogance and send your wrath upon their heads. Give into my hand, the hand of this widow, the strength to do what I have planned.
By the deceit of my lips strike down the slave along with the ruler, and the ruler along with his servant.

Destroy [?] those who rise up against them by the hand of a woman, so that all kingdoms may know that you are God. For your power and your strength are not in numbers, nor do your gifts [?] make anyone mighty. For you are the God of the lowly, the helper of the deprived, the support of the weak, the protector of the forsaken, the life of the helpless, the father of orphans.
Yes, O Lord of my father Simeon, God of the inheritance of Israel, Lord of heaven and earth, Creator of the seas and of all waters, King of all your creatures, hear my supplication.

Make my guile and deceit a wound and a scourge for the enemies. They are the enemies of your law, of your holy house, of the summit of Zion and of the temple that is the inheritance of your sons. They have planned to do a cruel deed against all your kindred.
Over all your tribes, look upon the true oath that you swore to Abraham, so that they may know you: that you are God, the God of power and strength, and that Israel has no other helper but you."
And it came to pass, when she had ceased crying out to the Lord, the God of Israel, and had finished all these words,
that she rose from where she had bowed down, called her maid, and went down into her house, where she used to stay on the sabbath days and on her feast days.

She took off the sackcloth she had been wearing and took off the clothes of her widowhood. She washed her body with water and anointed herself with rich ointment. She arranged the hair of her head to adorn it, put a headband on her head, and put on the festive clothes she used to wear during the life of Manasseh, her husband.
She put sandals on her feet and put on armlets, bands, rings, earrings and all her ornaments. She adorned herself so as to be very alluring to the eyes of any men who would see her.
She gave her maid a skin of wine and a jar of oil to carry. She filled a bag with parched grain, fig cakes, pure bread and cheese, packed all her vessels, and gave them to her to carry.
The two of them went out to the gates of the city of Bethulia, and they found Uzziah standing there with the elders of the city, Chabris and Charmis.
When they saw her, with her face altered and her clothing changed, they marveled greatly at her beauty and said to her:

"Go in peace, and may the Lord God be with you and go before you to take vengeance on our enemies! May the God of our fathers give you favor and accomplish your plan, to the glory of the children of Israel and the exaltation of Jerusalem!"

Judith bowed down on her face to God and said to them: "Now may the Lord God do according to your words, and may his handmaid find favor in his eyes. Now then, command that the gates of the city be opened for me, and I will go out to accomplish the things you spoke of with me." And they ordered the young men to open the gates for her, as she had told them.
Judith went out of the city, and her maid with her. The men of the city watched her until she had passed over the mountain.
As she went straight on through the valley, the Assyrian sentries met her.

They seized her and asked her: "Whose are you? Where do you come from, and where are you going?" Judith said to them: "I am a daughter of the Hebrews, and I am fleeing, for they are about to be given into your hands to be devoured.

I am coming before Holofernes, the commander of your army, to tell him words of truth. I will show him a way by which he may go in and become master of all this hill country, and not one man of them, not one body, not one living soul, will escape."
When the men heard these words, they looked closely at her face. Her beauty seemed very wonderful to them, and they said to her:
"You have saved your life well by hastening to come down and meet the face of our lord. Now go to his tent, and some of us will take you there until they hand you over to him.
And when you stand before him, do not let your heart be afraid, but tell him everything just as you have said, and it will go well with you!"
They chose a hundred of their men, entrusted her and her maid to them, and they led them to the tent of Holofernes.

And everyone in his camp came running, because news of her arrival had reached the whole gathering. They came and gazed at her and stood around her while she was still standing outside the tent of Holofernes, and they told him about her.

And they marvelled at her beauty. They brought her in and accepted her words, because her words were very good, and they marvelled at the Israelites because of her. Each man said to his neighbour: "Who can despise this people, who have women like these among them? It is not right to leave even one of them alive, because those who are left will be able to outwit [?] the whole earth."
And all the guards of Holofernes and his servants came out and brought her into his tent.
Holofernes was lying on his bed, resting under the canopy, which was made of purple and woven with gold, emerald and precious carbuncle.
They told him everything about her, and Holofernes came out into the forecourt of the tent with silver lamps carried before him.
When Judith came before him and his servants, they marvelled at the beauty of her face. She fell on her face and bowed down to him, and his slaves raised her up.
Holofernes said to her: "Do not be afraid, woman. Take courage in your heart, because I have never harmed any man who chose to serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of all the earth.
Now as for your people who live in the hill country: they despised me. I did not raise my spear against them; they brought this on themselves.
Now tell me, why did you flee from them and come to us? You have come to save your life. Do not be afraid. You will live through this night, and from now on
no one will harm you. Instead you will be treated well, as the servants of my lord Nebuchadnezzar are treated well."
Judith said to him: "Listen to your maidservant and let your servant speak, and she will tell no lie to my lord this night.

If you follow the words of your maidservant, God will bring the matter to completion with you. God will accomplish a great deed by your hand, and my lord will not fail in his undertakings as long as he lives.

For as Nebuchadnezzar lives, king of all the earth, and as his power lives, who has sent you to govern every living soul: through you not only do men serve him, but the wild beasts of the field, the cattle and the birds of the sky will also live by your strength. And Nebuchadnezzar and all his household will know

that we have heard of your wisdom and the shrewdness of your heart. It has been reported throughout the whole earth that you alone are the best man in all his kingdom, mighty in knowledge and wonderful in the command of war.

And now, lord, as for what Achior said in your council: we have heard his words. The men of Bethulia took him in, and he told them what he had said in front of you, and also the words that you had spoken.

Therefore, my lord and master, do not pass over his words, but lay them up in your heart, for they are true. Our nation cannot be punished by anyone, and the sword does not prevail over them, unless they sin against their God. Therefore, my lord and master, do not pass over his words, but lay them up in your heart, for they are true. Our nation cannot be punished by anyone, and the sword does not prevail over them, unless they sin against their God.

And now, so that the Lord my God may not be left outside and idle in this matter, let death fall upon them. For a great sin has overtaken them, by which they will anger their God, they who have committed lawlessness. And now, so that the Lord my God may not be left outside and idle in this matter, let death fall upon them. For a great sin has overtaken them, by which they will anger their God, they who have committed lawlessness.

For their food has run out, and they have used up all their water for drinking. They have resolved to lay hands even on their livestock, and they have set their hearts on eating everything that God commanded in his law not to be eaten. For their food has run out, and they have used up all their water for drinking. They have resolved to lay hands even on their livestock, and they have set their hearts on eating everything that God commanded in his law not to be eaten.

And they have decided to consume the offering of wheat and the tithe of wine and oil, which was set aside and consecrated for the priests who stand in Jerusalem before the face of our God. It is not lawful for any of them even to touch these with the hand, except the priest alone. And they have decided to consume the offering of wheat and the tithe of wine and oil, which was set aside and consecrated for the priests who stand in Jerusalem before the face of our God. It is not lawful for any of them even to touch these with the hand, except the priest alone.

And they have not sent anything as an offering to Jerusalem. For this reason those who live there have perceived this, those whom they [?] there for a release from the elders. And they have not sent anything as an offering to Jerusalem. For this reason those who live there have perceived this, those whom they [?] there for a release from the elders.

And it will be that when it is reported to them and they do not do it, they will be given into your hands to be destroyed, you would say [?]. And it will be that when it is reported to them and they do not do it, they will be given into your hands to be destroyed, to be told to you [?].
And these words of hers pleased Holofernes and all his servants. They marveled at her wisdom and said:
There is no woman like this from one end of the earth to the other, for beauty of face and for understanding in speech.
And Holofernes said to her: God has done well in sending you ahead of the people, so that strength may come by my hand, and destruction to those who have despised my lord.

And now you are striking in your appearance and good in your speech. If you do as you have said, your God shall be my God. You shall sit in the house of King Nebuchadnezzar, and you shall be renowned above all the earth.
And he ordered that she be brought in where his silver was stored. He commanded that her [?] be placed there, and that she be given some of his provisions and some of his wine to drink.
And Judith said: "I will not eat any of it, nor drink, so that it may not become a stumbling block for me. What I have brought with me will be enough for me."
And Holofernes said to her: "If what you have runs out, where will we get you more like it? There is no one with us from your people."
And Judith said to him: "As your soul lives, my lord, your handmaid will not use up what I have with me before God does by my hand what he has planned."
And Holofernes' servants brought her into the tent, and she slept until midday. She rose at dawn, right at the time of the incense offering.
And she sent word to Holofernes, saying: "Let my lord command that his handmaid be allowed to go out."
And Holofernes commanded his guards not to stop her. She stayed in the camp for three days. Each night she would go out to the valley of Bethulia and wash at the spring of water that was by the camp.
And when she came up from bathing, she would pray to the Lord God of Israel to direct her way for the raising up of the children of her people Israel.
And she would go in and stay in the tent until she received her food in the evening.
And on the fourth day Holofernes held a drinking feast with his servants, but he did not invite anyone according to rank, as was proper.
And he said to Bagoas, his eunuch, who was in charge of all his servants: "Go and persuade the Hebrew woman who is in your care to come to us.
Look, it will be a disgrace to us if we let such a woman go like this. If we leave her alone and do not talk with her, and if we do not win her over to us, people will mock us."

And Bagoas went out from Holofernes' presence, went in to her, and said: "Let this good handmaid not hesitate to come to my lord, so that you may be honoured before him, drink wine with us in gladness, and be with us this day like one of the daughters of the Assyrians who serve in the house of Nebuchadnezzar."
And Judith said to him: "And who am I to refuse my lord? Whatever is pleasing in his eyes I will do quickly, and it will be a joy to me until the day of my death."

And she got up and put on her garments and all her women's finery. Her handmaid went ahead of her and spread on the ground for her, in front of Holofernes, the sheepskin that she had received from Bagoas for Judith's own use, so that she could sit on it at meals.

And Judith came in and sat down. Holofernes' heart was overwhelmed by her, and his soul was stirred. His heart longed greatly to be with her, for he had been watching for an opportunity to seduce her from the day he first saw her.
And Holofernes said to her: "Drink, and be merry with us."
And Judith said to him: "I will drink now, my lord, for my life has been made greater in me than in all the days since I was born."
She took what her handmaid had prepared for her and ate and drank it in front of him.
And Holofernes was delighted with her and drank a great deal of wine, more than he had ever drunk on any single day of his life.

When evening came, his servants hurried off to their own quarters. Bagoas shut the tent door from outside and sent the attendants away from his lord's presence. They all went to their tents, because they were all tired and drunk, since the drinking had gone on a long time.
Judith was left alone in the tent. Holofernes lay sprawled on his bed, because the wine had overcome him.

Judith told her maidservant to stand outside her bedchamber and watch for her to come out, so that no one would come near her, as on every other day. She had said that she would go out to her prayer, and she had told Bagoas the same thing.

Everyone left, and no one, small or great, remained in the bedchamber. Judith stood beside his bed and said in her heart: "O Lord, God of all power, look at this hour on the work of my hands, for the exaltation of Jerusalem.
For now is the time to help your inheritance and to carry out my plan to destroy our enemies, who have risen up against us. Strengthen me, O God of Israel, this day!"
She went to the bedpost at Holofernes' head and took his sword down from it.
She came close to the bed, took hold of the hair of his head and said: "Strengthen me, O God of Israel, this day!"
Then she struck his neck twice with all her strength and cut off his head.
She rolled his body off the bed and took the canopy down from the posts. Shortly after this she went out and gave Holofernes' head to her maidservant.

The maidservant put it in the food bag. Then the two of them went out together, as they usually did for prayer. They passed through the camp, went all the way around the ravine, climbed the mountain of Bethulia and reached its gates.
From a distance Judith called to the gatekeepers: "Open, open the gates for me! For our God is with us, to show his power again in Israel and his strength against our enemies, as he has done today."
When the men of the city heard her voice, they hurried down to the city gates and called the elders of the city.
They all came running, small and great, because her return seemed a marvel to them. They opened the gates and let the two women in. They lit a fire to give light and gathered around them.
She said to them: "Praise the Lord, praise him, praise God, who has not taken his mercy away from the house of Israel, but has destroyed our enemies by my hand this night!"

Then she took Holofernes' head out of the bag, showed it to them and said: "Here is the head of Holofernes, commander-in-chief of the Assyrian army, and here is his covering, which he lay under in his drunkenness. The Lord has struck him down by the hand of a woman."

And the Lord God lives, who protected me on my way, the way on which I had gone, before his glory. He gave him into the hand of a woman: Holofernes, who spoke richly [?]. For my face deceived him to his destruction, and he plotted with me to sin and to defile me, the shame of filthiness. But I trusted in the Lord with my whole heart and with the will of my soul. And the Lord, who protected Sarah from the lust of Pharaoh and delivered Rebekah from Abimelech, has also rescued me, his handmaid, from the hand of the Assyrians and of their ruler.

And all the people were greatly amazed, and they bent their knees. They worshipped God and all said together: "Blessed are you, O Lord God of our fathers, who on this very day have put the enemies of your people to shame by the hand of a woman."

And Uzziah said to her: "Blessed are you, daughter, by God Most High, above all the women of the earth. And blessed is the Lord God, who made the heavens and the earth, who guided you to strike the head of the ruler of our enemy."
"For your praise will not be forgotten from the hearts of men, and they will remember the power of God forever."

"And may God make this an everlasting exaltation for you, and may he look upon you with good things, because you did not spare even your own life on account of the humiliation of our people. Instead you went out [?] against our ruin and walked in uprightness before our God." And all the people said: "So be it, so be it!"
And Judith said: "Hear me, brothers. Take this head and hang it on the battlement of your wall." And when the camp, those who were in the tents, heard of it, they were astonished at that matter.

"And when dawn breaks and the sun comes out over the earth, let each man take up his weapon of war. Go out, every strong man, outside the city, and set a commander over them, as if you were going down to the plain against the outpost [?] of the sons of the Assyrians, but do not go down." And fear and trembling fell upon them, and no man stood before the face of his neighbour; they all scattered together. And they fled by every road of the plain and of the hill country.

"And they will take up their weapons and go to their camp, and they will rouse the commanders of the Assyrian army. They will run to the tent of Holofernes and will not find him. And great fear will fall upon them, and they will flee from before you." Those who were encamped on the mountain around Bethulia set out in flight. And then the sons of Israel, every warrior among them, poured out upon them in pursuit.

"And you follow them, you and all the inhabitants of all the territories of Israel, and strike them down on their roads!" And Uzziah sent messengers to Bethomasthaim, to Abelmaim [?], to Choba and to Kola, and to all the territories of Israel, to report everything that had happened, so that all might pour out upon their enemies to destroy them.

"And before this happens, call Achior the Ammonite here, so that he may see and recognize the one who despised the name of Israel and sent him to us as one condemned to death." And when the sons of Israel heard this, they all poured out against them together and struck them down with a very great slaughter throughout those villages as far as Choba. And the people of Jerusalem came with them, and from all the hill country round about, for they had been told what had happened in the camp of their enemies. And those who were in Gilead prevailed over them even more, and those who were in Galilee pursued them. And there was a great slaughter of the Assyrians until they passed Damascus and its borders.

And they brought Achior from the house of Uzziah. And when he came and saw the head of Holofernes in the hands of one man in the midst of the assembly of the people, he fell on his face and fainted. But the other inhabitants of Bethulia fell upon the camp of the Assyrians and plundered them, and became very greatly rich.

And when they raised him up, he fell at Judith's feet and bowed down on his face before her and said to her: "Blessed are you among all the tribes of Ephraim, for those who hear your name will tremble, and shame will seize them." And the sons of Israel returned from slaughtering them, and they fell upon all who were left. And the cities and villages of the hill country and of all the plains came down, and they carried off much plunder, for there was a very great quantity of it.

"But now tell us, how much have you done in these days?" And Judith told him, in the midst of the people, everything she had done; she related to them everything from the day she went out. And Joakim the high priest came, with the elders of the sons of Israel who lived in Jerusalem; they all came to see the good things that the Lord had done for Israel, and to see Judith and to speak peace with her.

And when she finished speaking, the people shouted with a loud voice and raised a sound of rejoicing in their city. And when they came to her, they all blessed her together and said to her: "You are the exaltation of Jerusalem, you are the joy of Israel, you are the great pride of our nation."

And when Achior saw all that God had done for Israel, he believed in God and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and he was added to the house of Israel to this day. "You who have done all this with your own hand and have done good for Israel, and God has been pleased with them: may you be blessed by the Lord Almighty forever and ever." And all the people said: "So be it, so be it!"

And just as dawn was breaking, they hung the head of Holofernes on the wall, and every man took up his weapons, and they went up company by company to the ascent of the mountain. And the people [?] plundered the camp of the Assyrians for thirty days, and they gave Judith the tent of Holofernes and all his silver, his couches, his bedding, and his clothing. And she took it and loaded it onto her mules, piled it onto her wagons, and took all of it away from them.

When the sons of the Assyrians saw them, they sent word around to their leaders, to their commanders, to their captains of thousands and to all their rulers. All the women of Israel hurried to see her and to bless her, and they performed dances among them in her honour. They took branches of trees and put them in her hands, and they also gave crowns of olive to the women who were with her.

They went to Holofernes' tent and said to Bagoas, who was in charge of his whole household: "Wake our lord, for the slaves have dared to come down and fight against us, so that they may be utterly destroyed." And she led all the people in the dance, going before all the women. Every man of Israel followed them, armed and wearing crowns, singing hymns with their mouths.

Bagoas went in and knocked at the court of the tent, because he supposed that he was still sleeping with Judith. And Judith led all the people in this song of thanksgiving, and all the people responded with this praise.
When no one answered, he waited a while and then went into the bedchamber. He found him lying dead beneath the bed, and his head had been cut off from him.
He cried out with weeping, with a loud voice and with great lamentation, and he tore his garments.
He went into the tent where Judith used to stay as her lodging, and he did not find her. He ran out to the people and cried out, saying:

"His slaves have acted with contempt and have done a shameful thing! One Hebrew woman has won a victory over the house of Nebuchadnezzar. Look, Holofernes is lying on the ground, and his head is not with him!"

When the leaders of that mighty Assyrian people heard these words, they tore their garments, and their spirits were greatly dismayed. Their cry and their lamentation among their people were very great.
And Judith said: "Praise my God with tambourines, and sing to the Lord with the sound of cymbals. Sing to him in harmony a new psalm, and exalt him and call upon his name,
for he is the one who crushes wars; the Lord is his name. It is God who struck down their camp in the midst of his people and rescued me from the hands of my pursuers.
For the Assyrian came from the mountains of the north. He came with the myriads of his army. Their multitude blocked up the valleys and dried up the waters, and their horses covered the hills.
He said he would burn my borders, kill my young men with the sword, dash my nursing infants to the ground, give my little children up as plunder, and carry my virgins away captive.
The Lord Almighty has humiliated them by the hand of a woman and put them to shame.

For their mighty one did not fall at the hands of young men. He was not slain by Titans, and tall giants did not strike him down. Instead, Judith, daughter of Merari, undid them by the beauty of her face.
For she took off her widow's garments for the exaltation of those who laboured in Israel. She anointed her face with perfumed ointment,
bound up her hair with a headdress, and put on a linen garment to deceive him.
Her sandals ravished his eyes, her beauty took his soul captive, and the sword passed through his neck.
The Persians trembled at her boldness, and the [?] (probably the Medes) at her daring. The whole camp of the Assyrians trembled, and they fell.
Then my lowly ones cried out, and the weak were afraid at my distress; they were thrown into confusion and raised their voice, and my enemies were turned back.
The sons of maidens pierced them through, and they slaughtered them like fleeing boys, and they perished by the mercy of my Lord.
I will sing to my God a new song: Lord, Lord, you are great in power and glorious in wonders.
Let all your creatures serve you, for you spoke, and so they came to be; you sent forth your word, and they were built; and there is no one who can stand against your voice.
For the mountains were shaken from their foundations together with the waters, and the rocks melted like wax before your face. Yet you will again show mercy to those who fear you,
for every sacrifice for a sweet-smelling fragrance is a small thing, and all fat for an offering to you is the least of things. But whoever fears the Lord is great forever.

Woe to the nations that rise up against my people! The Lord Almighty will take vengeance on them in the day of judgment and will visit them. He will give fire and worms to their flesh, and they will weep in their pain forever and ever.

And when they came to Jerusalem and worshipped God, once the people had been purified from their uncleanness, they offered their sacrifices to the Lord, along with their vows, their freewill offerings and their gifts.
And Judith gave all the vessels of Holofernes, as many as the people had given her, and she gave the canopy that she had taken from his bedchamber as an offering to the Lord.
And the people rejoiced before the Lord in Jerusalem, in front of the sanctuary, for three months, and Judith stayed with them, together with her possessions.
After those days each one set out and went home to his own inheritance. And Judith went to Bethulia and lived on her property, and in her time she was renowned throughout the whole land.
And no man saw her all the days of her life, from the day that Manasseh her husband died and was gathered to his people.

And she grew in honour and became very great, and she grew old in her husband's house and lived one hundred and five years. She set her maidservant free and gave her a share of her possessions. And she died in Bethulia, and they buried her in the tomb of Manasseh her husband.

And the whole house of Israel mourned for her for seven days. Before her death she had divided her possessions among all the close relatives of Manasseh her husband and the close relatives of her own family.
And there was no longer anyone who made the children of Israel afraid in the days of Judith, nor for many days after her death.
